articles.title: Trump floats ‘big decision’ at UN on whether he’ll ‘annihilate’ Iran or make deal
articles.summary: President Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that he has a major decision coming on the U.S. war in Iran and predicted a deal could be reached between the two countries after November’s midterm elections. “I have a big decision to make,” Trump told the international body, including Iranian representatives. ”Will a…
articles.body:
President Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that he has a major decision coming on the U.S. war in Iran and predicted a deal could be reached between the two countries after November’s midterm elections.

“I have a big decision to make,” Trump told the international body, including Iranian representatives. ”Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever war before. Maybe the greatest in the Middle East or even the world.”

“Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again. Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he continued.

Trump went on to say he believes the two countries will make a deal after the elections.

“Because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” he said.

“They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election. What they don’t realize is that I’m not running. I did that already, and won in a landslide,” he said, noting he will be in the presidency for two and a half more years.

Trump said he gives “absolutely no credence” to the midterms when it comes to Iran.

“It doesn’t even enter my mind. The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” the president said to applause.

Trump’s address comes as the U.S. continues to be hit hard by rising energy prices as a result of the war in Iran. According to AAA, the national average for gas prices sat at $4.47 while diesel was at $6.52.

A growing number of Republicans are breaking with Trump on the war, with frontline Senate candidates in Iowa and Michigan making calls to end the war or provide immediate economic relief on Monday.

The president has seen his approval rating drop to record lows, with a Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Monday showing Trump’s approval at 32 percent. Republicans running in the midterms are also struggling in the polls, trailing Democrats on the generic ballot.

Trump committed the most time during his speech to the war in Iran, but also touted his interventions in Venezuela, Cuba, Greenland and efforts to end war in Gaza and Ukraine.

Throughout his comments, the UN’s live stream of the address cut to a lone Iranian representative sitting in the chamber.

The Iranian delegation to the assembly includes its president, Masoud Pezeshkian, and foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that while nothing is scheduled, Trump would be open to meeting with Iranian officials at the international gathering.

Trump has a jam-packed schedule on Tuesday at the United Nations.

The president is slated to meet with a number of international leaders including the U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Immediately following his address, he joined the leaders of Greenland and Denmark for a new security agreement.

articles.title: Ocasio-Cortez on possible White House bid: ‘Pretty candidly, I think about my identity’
articles.summary: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), one of the most prominent Democrats of the last decade, discussed a 2028 presidential run and reflected on how her identity may impact her potential campaign. “I think about it personally,” Ocasio-Cortez told The New York Times in an interview published Tuesday, talking about a bid for the presidency. “I am…
articles.body:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), one of the most prominent Democrats of the last decade, discussed a 2028 presidential run and reflected on how her identity may impact her potential campaign.

“I think about it personally,” Ocasio-Cortez told The New York Times in an interview published Tuesday, talking about a bid for the presidency. “I am 36, I’m about to turn 37 years old — and what that means for my life.”

“Pretty candidly, I think about my identity,” the New York Democrat added. “I’m not naïve to the fact that we are living under a very regressive administration, and I happen to be a woman, and I, you know, happen to be Latina. And I think that there’s a lot of conversation about electability, and I don’t kind of shy away from those realities.”

Ocasio-Cortez has been one of the most-discussed names as a possible 2028 White House contender. And the ascendancy of fellow democratic socialists and progressives in recent Democratic primaries could bolster a case for her presidential candidacy.

In the Times interview, Ocasio-Cortez said she’ll make a choice on whether to make a presidential bid following this year’s midterms.

Some influential Democrats’ confidence has recently increased about Ocasio-Cortez’s chances in the upcoming presidential race. Multiple members of her party have even compared her rise to former President Obama’s insurgent 2008 campaign and the on-the-ground support that sent him to the White House.

The New York Democrat has also been notably vulnerable in the political spotlight recently, announcing a decision to freeze her eggs and documenting the process on social media.

articles.title: Jeffries lashes out after House Dem bolsters Republican candidate on leader's home turf
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries called Mike Lawler a "partisan hack" after Jared Golden crossed party lines to endorse the Hudson Valley Republican for re-election.
articles.body: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is harshly dismissing a fellow Democrat who publicly undermined his quest to win the majority in Congress — on the left-wing leader's own home turf. Jeffries hit back at Rep. Jared Golden, D-Maine, in a statement to Fox News Digital on Tuesday after Golden endorsed Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., a moderate Republican, for re-election in November. "Mike Lawler is a partisan hack and Trump sycophant who Cait Conley will defeat in November. In desperation, he is peddling an 11th-hour endorsement from a retiring congressmember who represents an out-of-town district more than 400 miles away," Jeffries said. "This smoke-and-mirrors ploy will do nothing to change the outcome of the race. The election will be decided by the people of Westchester and the lower Hudson Valley." OUTGOING HOUSE DEMOCRAT BACKS INCUMBENT REPUBLICAN LAWMAKER FOR RE-ELECTION Jeffries claimed Lawler had "never shown bipartisan courage when it matters" while lauding his Democrat opponent as a "combat veteran and patriot." DEMOCRAT CHALLENGING MIKE LAWLER WON'T COMMIT ON CAMPAIGNING WITH AOC, MAMDANI OR REJECTING DSA "Mike Lawler can try to run from his extremist record. We will never let him hide," he said. But Golden, who has broken from Jeffries multiple times in the past, argued Lawler was among the most bipartisan members of Congress. JEFFRIES THREATENS 'SERIOUS RESPONSE' AFTER DEMOCRATS HELP GOP ADVANCE ANTI-SOCIALISM VOTE "I know how bipartisan Mike Lawler really is. I know something about what that takes. I held the most challenging district of any Democrat in the country by earning the trust of Democrats, independents, and Republicans alike," Golden wrote. "Lawler holds one of just three Republican seats in the country that Kamala Harris carried in 2024. Representing districts like ours forces you to work for people who disagree with you, and it teaches you that those people are not your enemies. They are your neighbors." HOUSE DEMS OVERWHELMINGLY REJECT ANTI-SOCIALISM RESOLUTION AFTER 2 MODERATES DEFY JEFFRIES He pointed out that the nonpartisan Lugar Bipartisanship Index ranked Lawler the fourth-most bipartisan member of Congress in its most recent analysis. "I am leaving Congress in January by my own choice, but I have not given up on the institution, and voters should not either. The Congress we get is the one we elect, and the country needs fewer members who treat the job as a stage and more who treat it as work. In New York's Hudson Valley this fall, that is the choice on the ballot," Golden wrote. Lawler thanked Golden for the endorsement in his own public statement. "While we are from different parties and different states, Jared and I have worked during our time together in the House to find common ground on issues that matter both to us and our constituents," he wrote on X. "We share a firm belief that what’s best for the people should come before one’s party, and that if more members on both sides of the aisle took that approach more often, the country would be better off for it." Lawler is facing long odds of winning a third term in Congress, with most projections favoring Democrats in his district in the New York City suburbs. But Lawler has defied political gravity before, including most recently in November 2024 when his victory split the ticket with ex-Vice President Kamala Harris. DEMOCRATS PUNISH MEMBERS WHO PUT WORKING AMERICANS AHEAD OF PARTY LOYALTY Golden, who is retiring at the end of this year, is known for breaking from his party on a variety of issues. He was one of the only Democrats to praise President Donald Trump's tariff efforts. He also recently made headlines for publicly defying Jeffries by voting with Republicans on a procedural measure called a "rule vote" alongside fellow moderate Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash. While Republican lawmakers have weaponized rule votes in recent years to extract promises from House GOP leaders, it was almost unheard of for Democrats to defy their leaders like that on the other side of the aisle. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP It was especially stunning to see Golden and Perez do so twice within one month — with Jeffries attacking the move as a "breach of trust" the first time.

articles.title: Rubio defends Trump’s White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
articles.summary: The White House launched ‘Trump TV’ as major networks suspended the television pool covering the US president.
articles.body:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has defended US President Donald Trump’s decision to ban CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House, arguing that the administration has restricted their access to the presidential complex rather than their ability to operate as news organisations.

“We’re not closing CNN,” Rubio said in an interview on Tuesday with NBC. “There aren’t a bunch of police officers or soldiers kicking down the doors of MSNBC or MS NOW, whatever it’s called, and arresting people and unplugging it from the grid. They’re just not allowed to work from the workspace at the White House.”

Rubio is the latest senior administration official to defend the decision, after US Vice President JD Vance also backed the move.

“We’re not going to give you special access to the White House if you engage in what is effectively far-left propaganda,” Vance told reporters on Monday, arguing that the move was about “basic fairness”.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, meanwhile, said he told Trump during a meeting at Gracie Mansion on Monday that he wanted all members of the press present at the event.

“We’re going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn,” Mamdani said. “And that is something that I believe in – everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique that we engage.”

Trump announced the ban on Friday, accusing the three outlets of repeatedly publishing what he called “fake news” about his administration. The White House said the First Amendment of the US Constitution protects the right to publish but does not guarantee access to the White House, briefing room, or presidential press pool.

The decision was implemented on Saturday , when journalists from the three organisations were denied entry to the White House and had their access credentials revoked.

The outlets sued the administration on Monday, arguing that the ban violates their First Amendment rights and that the government cannot restrict journalists’ access because of their reporting. A federal judge is expected to consider their request for a temporary restraining order.

The dispute has also disrupted the White House television pool, which allows participating networks to share footage and other coverage when space limits the number of journalists who can attend presidential events. Major television networks withheld pool coverage of Trump on Monday after CNN was removed from the rotation.

That same evening, the White House launched “Trump TV”, a 24-hour streaming channel on YouTube and the White House website, featuring 24/7 video streaming of videos and speeches from the president. When it launched, the channel aired an archived Trump speech from July at Mount Rushmore.

“Get real-time updates and live events streamed DIRECTLY to your phone,” the White House wrote on social media. “No noise. Just the news that matters most — straight from the Trump Administration.”

images.caption: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump's ban of the three media outlets, saying, 'We're not closing down CNN' [Jeenah Moon/AFP]

articles.title: County GOP chair resigns over social media posts
articles.summary: The chairman of the Marquette County, Mich., Republican Party has resigned from his position amid growing scrutiny over social media posts where he reportedly expressed low Republican enthusiasm for the upcoming midterm elections. Jackson Karki, 19, resigned from his position after he was linked to the anonymous “Red Lion Politics” account on the social platform…
articles.body:
The chairman of the Marquette County, Mich., Republican Party has resigned from his position amid growing scrutiny over social media posts where he reportedly expressed low Republican enthusiasm for the upcoming midterm elections.

Jackson Karki, 19, resigned from his position after he was linked to the anonymous “Red Lion Politics” account on the social platform X.

“The vibes on the ground are the worst I’ve seen in my life. No one wants to promote candidates, no one wants to knock doors, no one wants to do s—,” Karki wrote on the account. “Attendance for any right wing event is at all time lows anywhere I go. Thank you Donald Trump for ruining it for us… and handing the country over to socialism.”

He also worked as the chairman of at least four Michigan counties for former Rep. Mike Rogers’s (R-Mich.) Senate bid, according Straight from The Hut .

“And as someone that has knock doors the energy of the people answering the doors is terrible as well,” he added .

Karki criticized the GOP in a statement to The Detroit News , writing, “the Republican Party is meant to be the party of debate, open discussion and integrity.”

“As of late, the party has become very tight-knit and, in some ways, the opposite of those things,” he continued. “I hope those inside the party start to realize what’s going on instead of being ignorant, because ignorance is the root of losing.”

Marquette County’s interim chairwoman Jennifer Jermalowicz also told the outlet that the organization was not aware that Karki “was making inflammatory comments about fellow Republicans,” including his remarks against Trump.

She confirmed that the organization’s leadership would be meeting on how to respond to Karki’s posts.

His words come as Rogers competes in a battleground election against progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Republicans took control of the district’s state House election seat in 2024. However in the same election, President Trump lost the county by around 3,000 votes to former Vice President Kamala Harris.

In a Suffolk University poll, El-Sayed held a 7-point lead against Rogers among 500 likely Michigan voters. Eleven percent of those surveyed said they were still unsure of their vote.

The Marquette County Republican Party did not respond immediately to The Hill’s request for comment.

articles.title: Looksmaxxer Clavicular charged with rape, reports say

( NewsNation ) — Looksmaxxer Clavicular has been charged with rape in Massachusetts, according to reports .

Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, is charged with one count of rape, one count of drugging someone for sexual intercourse and one count of procuring liquor for someone under 21, according to court records.

As an online personality, Clavicular focused on often-dangerous DIY aesthetic treatments intended to “ looksmax ,” or increase attractiveness. The concept of looksmaxxing grew out of the incel movement and emphasizes a hierarchy based on physical attractiveness.

He has been known for a practice called bone smashing, where he uses a hammer to deliberately break bones in his face to make them grow back stronger, something medical experts have warned against.

Charges were filed against Clavicular on Sept. 8, with records showing the date of the alleged offense as May 23, 2025. No other details were available.

The charges were first reported by the Bulwark , with a representative for Clavicular saying the report was exaggerated and that Clavicular had not been served an arrest warrant.

Clavicular was previously sued by a teenage influencer who accused him of battery, saying he arranged for her to go to Cape Cod, Massachusetts, got her drunk on vodka and had sex with her while intoxicated.

articles.title: Trump follows in Hugo Chavez’s footsteps to launch his own TV channel
articles.summary: Trump has launched his own channel amid an ongoing rift with the White House press pool.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump launched a round-the-clock YouTube channel run by the White House on Monday.

The move follows his banning of CNN, MS NOW (formerly MSNBC), and Politico from reporting from the White House on Friday, prompting five major television networks to suspend coverage on Monday morning in protest.

The spat has triggered a wave of lawsuits from broadcasters, with the president warning on Saturday that he might ban other outlets for broadcasting what he claims is “fake news”.

Alongside his own social media platform, Truth Social, Trump appears to be trying to bypass mainstream media. But is this possible, and has anyone tried it before?

‘Trump TV: The Essentials Station’ is not a conventional television network but a 24-hour online video stream.

There are no anchors, no reporters and no original journalism. Instead, it broadcasts speeches, administration announcements, ceremonial events and selected highlights from Trump’s presidency.

How did Trump’s latest feud with mainstream media begin?

On Friday, Trump said he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, prompting a flurry of condemnation from several major media outlets and media rights watchdogs.

On Truth Social, he accused the outlets of propagating “fake news”. He added that the outlets “constantly write or report fiction or lies” about the Trump administration, but did not give any examples.

On Monday, the banned outlets sued the Trump administration for denying them their First Amendment rights.

Trump responded to the suit in a statement posted on Truth Social, lashing out at what he called the “fake news people”, and saying that “the Oval Office … should be treated with Decorum, Respect, and Dignity, not defiled by Third Rate Clowns”.

“No matter how GREAT my Achievements, they trivialise and demean,” the president added.

The television news pool then announced it was suspending its coverage of the president’s events.

The White House broadcasting pool is made up of five networks – ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC. They take turns filming the president, providing live feeds that are picked up by the networks and outlets around the world.

When the White House blocked CNN from the rotation on Monday, the other four refused to replace the network.

The result was an awkward broadcast in which a White House ribbon-cutting ceremony attended by Trump, surrounded by workers in hard hats and safety vests, was broadcast by US news outlet Newsmax with only live visuals and no audio because no television press pool was present.

Other news outlets also showed solidarity with the press pool. The Associated Press (AP) joined several news organisations, including The Washington Post and The New York Times, in deciding not to publish photographs taken by the White House photography pool of presidential events on Monday.

The same day, Trump launched his own channel.

How has Trump tried to bypass mainstream media in the past?

Trump has long tried to bypass mainstream media by communicating directly, often in capital letters alongside AI-generated depictions of himself, on his own social media platform, Truth Social.

Last year, he also sought to bar AP reporters from the White House Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico – which lies partially in Mexican and other waters – to the Gulf of America. AP has taken legal action against this.

Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has pursued other legal actions against a variety of different outlets, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the BBC.

His administration is also involved in a long-simmering confrontation with ABC over renewal of its broadcast licences.

Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media.

Some outlets that he favours, such as Fox News and Newsmax, often carry his events in full, while podcasters and online streamers considered friendly to him often give him long, unedited interviews.

Have other leaders launched their own media channels?

Yes. One of the best-known examples is Venezuela’s former president Hugo Chavez.

From 1999 to 2012, he hosted Hello, President, a Sunday television and radio show that often ran for several hours per episode.

Chavez sang, took calls from viewers, attacked his opponents and sometimes announced major policy live on air.

He also made heavy use of cadenas, or broadcasts that all Venezuelan channels were legally required to carry at the same time.

Chavez’s successor, Nicolas Maduro, who US forces abducted and imprisoned on guns-and-drugs charges in January during a Trump-authorised lightning military raid on Caracas, kept the same model during his presidency.

He hosted his own weekly programme on state television, most recently called Con Maduro+, continued using cadenas, and became an active user of TikTok and other social media.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also followed a similar strategy.

Since 2014, he has hosted Words from the Heart, a monthly radio address via state broadcaster All India Radio, in which he talks directly to citizens without interviewers or questions.

He also has his own official NaMo app, through which he sends messages direct to the general public, rarely accepting questions directly from the press.

Brazil’s former President Jair Bolsonaro used Facebook Live during his 2019 to 2023 presidency, holding live weekly broadcasts, usually on Thursday evenings and often filmed in a casual setting at his official residence.

He used the broadcasts to make announcements, attack journalists and criticise Globo, Brazil’s largest media group.

El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele often announces major decisions on X rather than through press conferences.

In 2020, amid a dispute with independent outlets, he launched a government news programme on the state channel Canal 10 which broadcasts three times a day. His government also runs a daily newspaper dedicated to official messaging.

articles.title: Bill Clinton knocks Trump over arch, Kennedy Center moves
articles.summary: Former President Clinton is knocking President Trump’s plans for a triumphal arch and the efforts to put his name on the Kennedy Center, saying that global challenges would be more easily dealt with if leaders “didn’t care as much about who got the credit.” The 42nd president delivered opening remarks at the opening of the annual Clinton Global…
articles.body:
Former President Clinton is knocking President Trump’s plans for a triumphal arch and the efforts to put his name on the Kennedy Center, saying that global challenges would be more easily dealt with if leaders “didn’t care as much about who got the credit.”

The 42 nd president delivered opening remarks at the opening of the annual Clinton Global Initiative meeting in New York on Tuesday. As he took to the lectern, Clinton quickly referenced Trump’s recent announcement that plans for a massive arch bridging Washington and Virginia would incorporate a “top grade military complex” that would be used to store drones.

“I think it’s important to take a few minutes to assess where we are now and the environment in which we are meeting,” Clinton said.

“I suppose I could take my entire allotted time to discuss the self-evident wisdom of building an Arc de Triomphe in Washington to hold all our drones,” the former president said to laughs from the audience.

“Some of this stuff — it’s hard to make up,” he added.

“Over the course of a lifetime, there are only so many real opportunities to make decisions that we know will shape our personal history and the history of those we live with and care about for a long time to come. This is one of those moments,” he said, before mentioning the Kennedy Center board’s attempts to inscribe Trump’s name on the historic Washington building.

Last week, a federal judge blocked an effort by the Trump-picked board to add the president’s name to the institution and to rename its campus after Trump.

“I personally think that the way we’ve argued about what’s going on at the Kennedy Center and all that kind of stuff — I think we’ve been majoring in the minors,” Clinton said.

“You really think 100 years from now anybody’s going to care very much about whose name’s on what building?” he asked.

“Isn’t it more important what happens in the building? And what happens outside the building?” he continued.

“I feel so strongly — as I did 30 years ago-plus when I ran for president as a virtual child — that diversity is a positive thing, not a negative one.”

“That cooperation works better than conflict, and that we could actually deal with just about every challenge we face, if we didn’t care as much about who got the credit, and we made sure that we took care of the least of these,” Clinton, 80, said.

His remarks largely focused on dealing with the development of artificial intelligence and criticizing “zero-sum thinking” by the country’s political leaders.

“I believe that on the 250th anniversary of this country, we can’t have a politics driven by zero-sum thinking: In order for me to win, you have to lose,” he said.

“Nevertheless, I do understand why so many leaders around the world have chosen this zero-sum approach. Think how richly they have been rewarded for it in every sense of the word, and this payoff has been more apparent in the United States than any other country,” the former commander in chief said.

“Some days I can hardly believe what is happening in this country that I love so much. People in charge have created one set of rules for themselves and another set for everyone else,” Clinton said, without mentioning Trump by name.

“They’ve weaponized government to settle personal scores, prosecute enemies, stamp out free speech. They’ve even made the federal government a new profit center for themselves and their allies,” he said.

“That violates the spirit and letter of the Emoluments Clause of our Constitution.”

articles.title: Trump says AI will be renamed ‘super intelligence’ in all US documents
articles.summary: President Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that artificial intelligence will be renamed “super intelligence” in all U.S. documents. “The United States also totally rejects any attempt to construct a globality scheme to control for the artificial intelligence being spoken of so much now, hereinafter called super intelligence. Changing the name,” Trump…
articles.body:
President Trump told the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that artificial intelligence will be renamed “super intelligence” in all U.S. documents.

“The United States also totally rejects any attempt to construct a globality scheme to control for the artificial intelligence being spoken of so much now, hereinafter called super intelligence. Changing the name,” Trump told the global body.

“The use of the word artificial makes intelligence sound fake,” he continued. “It is not fake. It’s actually amazing. But we have to be careful. In fact, it is exactly the opposite of what it purports.”

“From this point forward, all of United States documents and hopefully the world’s will be changed to use the much more accurate term super as opposed to artificial,” he continued.

“In other words, welcome to the new world of super intelligence — SI,” he said. “Let’s see if that goes. It sounds much better. It is much better, and it’s much more accurate.”

Super intelligence is already defined as a form of artificial intelligence that exceeds human intelligence. It is both the ultimate goal of many frontier AI firms and the greatest worry among those warning about its threat to humanity.

Trump’s remarks came amid spiking fears about the technology after a former Anthropic researcher warned that AI could soon destroy humanity.

The concerns fueled the debate in Washington over whether to regulate the technology, with Trump pushing for less regulation to ensure the U.S. beats China in the AI arms race.

AI is slated to be a major topic of conversation this week, not only at the United Nations General Assembly but also when Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit with Trump.

articles.title: Federal appeals court orders Missouri to use congressional map rejected twice by Supreme Court
articles.summary: A Missouri appeals court ordered use of a GOP-drawn congressional map that splits Kansas City's district, but opponents say ballots are printed.
articles.body: A Missouri appeals court ordered Monday that the state must use a GOP-drawn congressional map in November’s elections, reversing a series of Supreme Court decisions. The St. Louis-based Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals made the ruling Monday, just one day before absentee and mail-in ballots were slated to be sent out to voters. Military and overseas voters have already begun to receive ballots, according to the Associated Press. "This Court holds that Missouri’s current plan to use the 2022 map in the November 2026 general election violates the Constitution. Only use of the 2025 map complies with the Constitution and federal law," Eighth Circuit Judge Stephen R. Clark wrote in a previous decision, which was upheld by the appeals panel in Monday's ruling. The map, drawn by Missouri’s Republican-dominated state assembly in 2025, has already been rejected by the U.S. Supreme Court twice on procedural grounds, most recently earlier this month. ELECTION CHAOS IN THIS RED STATE JUST GOT EVEN STRANGER FOR REPUBLICANS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING The new map splits Missouri’s 5th Congressional District, which encompasses the state’s largest metropolitan area centered on Kansas City, into two districts, likely eliminating one of the state’s two Democratic-leaning districts. Despite numerous challenges, Missouri did use the 2025 map for its August primary elections. An August ruling from a state trial court ruled that a reversion to the 2022 map "would move hundreds of thousands of voters into different districts for the imminent 2026 general election compared to the districts in which they cast their ballots in the August primary elections." The Missouri Association of County Clerks and Election Authorities already announced it won’t be using the 2025 map for November, arguing in an appeal filing that the state does not have enough time to provide new ballots, according to the AP. MISSOURI SUPREME COURT THREATENS SECRETARY OF STATE WITH CONTEMPT AMID INTENSIFYING REDISTRICTING BATTLE Opponents of the redrawn map, like People Not Politicians executive director Richard von Glahn, echoed that sentiment. "Ballots have been printed, and Missourians have already voted. Thousands more will vote before this order seeks to take effect. Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections," Glahn said in a statement issued to the AP. SUPREME COURT ALLOWS ALABAMA GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAP FOR MIDTERMS The appeals panel, however, argued that there is precedent to offering new ballots in such a short time period. The panel delayed its ruling from taking place for one week, allowing opponents to appeal to the Supreme Court again. MISSOURI JUDGE HANDS TRUMP, GOP MAJOR REDISTRICTING WIN AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS President Donald Trump has been a strong proponent of the redrawn map, blasting the early September decision by Missouri's Supreme Court to favor the 2022 maps. "The Missouri Supreme Court just ridiculously ruled in favor of changing the maps back to what they were a long time ago. It's called, Ancient History! The problem is, according to Legal Scholars, that not only was the ruling horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional, but there won't be enough time to change the map back with the Election coming up in a very short period of time," Trump wrote in a Sept. 4 post on Truth Social. "The Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America! Missouri must be able to use the map that was in effect just a couple of months ago, in the Primary. This is a Dark Day for 'Justice' in Missouri!" he wrote. articles.title: Trump flexes American power at UN with warnings to rivals around the globe
articles.summary: Trump told the United Nations the U.S. will rename artificial intelligence to "superintelligence" and reject any globalist scheme to control the tech.
articles.body: President Donald Trump told world leaders Tuesday that the U.S. is growing stronger economically, militarily and technologically, using his United Nations address to tout America’s lead in artificial intelligence and its expanding power abroad. "From this point forward, all of the United States documents and hopefully the world's will be changed to use the much more accurate term super as opposed to artificial. So it's super intelligence," said Trump. "Welcome to the new world of superintelligence," the president added. "Every major new technology brings challenges, and super intelligence is no exception," said Trump. "Whoever wins super intelligence wins. That's the group that wins. And we're leading now over China by a lot and everyone else. And we're going to keep it that way." Speaking before world leaders at the U.N. General Assembly in New York, Trump used the address to make a broader case for American strength, pointing to the war with Iran, pushing other countries to isolate Tehran economically and highlighting a deal that expands the U.S. military presence in Greenland. TRUMP TO ZERO-IN ON IRAN NUCLEAR THREAT, GAZA PLAN AND UN OVERHAUL IN WORLD STAGE SPEECH After months of failed negotiations and continued fighting between the U.S. and Iran, Trump predicted Tehran would reach a deal with Washington after the November midterm elections. "I believe we'll make a deal right after the election, because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election. What they don't realize is that I'm not running. I did that already and won in a landslide," said Trump. Trump said he inherited the Iran problem from previous administrations and argued that U.S. military action prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, saying European nations should recognize that they also benefited from the move. "I hope the Europeans realize that Iran's goal was to complete their mad dash to a nuclear bomb from behind this conventional ballistic missile shield," said Trump. "If they had succeeded, that wicked regime would have been free to spread terror and death forever, knowing that any attempt to stop them would face an arsenal." He thanked the U.N. Security Council for its resolution condemning Iran’s attacks on commercial shipping, then called on "all nations" to join the U.S. in a "complete economic isolation of Iran." WALTZ DELIVERS BLUNT WARNING TO NATIONS DEFYING IRAN SANCTIONS, TOUTS GREENLAND DEAL First lady Melania Trump, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz all were present for the speech. Trump also put Cuba on notice during his speech, declaring there will be "fundamental change" in the communist country following negotiations between Rubio and Cuban officials. AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI — CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD "Communism will never be coming to America, but freedom will be coming to Cuba," said Trump. Trump said that the U.S. will not allow foreign adversaries to threaten America at its own "doorstep." "The Cuban regime has also spent decades coordinating with the left-wing radicals and communist networks here in the United States. As our State Department has detailed, they've cultivated ties to subversive and radical groups such as the Communist Party USA, Antifa and the Democrat Socialists of America," said the president. Cuban officials exited the room when Trump declared Cuba a "failed state," leaving empty seats in their row. Trump touted the U.S. economy as the "envy" of the world with jobs rising, poverty reaching new lows and tax cuts. "The entire world is being lifted by the wealth, strength, spirit and momentum of a newly energized and a very powerful United States of America," said Trump. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Trump returned to drawing a clear line on putting America first, calling out the International Maritime Organization for "secretly establishing a first ever global carbon tax very expensive tax to raise international shipping costs." "There is no global government. And while I'm president, there will be no global taxes," he said. The administration recently announced a trilateral U.S.-Denmark-Greenland security agreement Friday. "No U.S. adversary will ever be permitted to establish a military presence in Greenland anymore or make sensitive investments there. Without our express written approval," said Trump, adding that the U.S. will build two military bases. Trump is set to meet with Prime Minister Frederiksen of Denmark and Prime Minister Nielsen of Greenland to sign the agreement following his remarks.

articles.title: Trump Jr under scrutiny from own party over Putin-linked oligarch's lavish gift
articles.summary: Republican Sen. John Curtis wants the Senate Judiciary Committee to subpoena both Donald Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden over alleged corruption tied to their fathers.
articles.body: A Senate Republican is going after a new target to battle corruption: Donald Trump Jr. Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, is pushing the Senate Judiciary Committee, led by Sen. Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, to launch investigations into Trump Jr. and Hunter Biden, a familiar target for the GOP. He wants both subpoenaed, and for both to testify before the panel over alleged foreign business dealings and corruption bolstered by their fathers’ status. In a letter to Grassley, Curtis argued that serious questions had come up about presidential family members using the influence of their presidential patriarch to boost their business dealings. TRUMP-BACKED CRYPTO BILL FAILS TO LAUNCH AS DEMS, REPUBLICANS UNITE TO BLOCK IT Those questions started with Biden and his alleged use of former President Joe Biden as an access point and have continued following reports of Trump Jr.’s lavish wedding after-party on a private island provided by a Russian oligarch."A toaster is a wedding gift," Curtis said on X highlighting his letter. "A private-island party paid for by a Putin-connected oligarch is something else. Republicans nearly wore out the subpoena machine investigating Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships. We should not unplug it now. ‘Trust us’ was not enough then, and it is not enough now." In the letter, Curtis contended that the concerns over Trump Jr.'s dealings "are compounded by Donald Trump Jr.’s active promotion of family-backed cryptocurrency ventures, his continued pursuit of international real estate deals involving direct meetings with foreign heads of state, and his reported investments in defense contracting." "This pattern extends to his significant financial and advisory ties to prediction market platforms that depend on favorable federal regulatory decisions being considered by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission," he continued. DONALD TRUMP JR AND BETTINA ANDERSON CELEBRATE PRIVATE WEDDING IN BAHAMAS, SHARE SWEET PERSONAL PHOTO The wedding party in May, first reported by ProPublica, was allegedly bankrolled by a Russian oligarch with close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin that Trump Jr. had recently met, and who has ties to the scandal-ridden International Boxing Association that is funded, in part, by the Russian state-owned energy company Gazprom. Trump Jr. has also been a key figure in boosting his father’s wealth. The president’s income between 2024 and 2025 ballooned by about 250% — from just over $620 million to about $2.2 billion, thanks in large part to his various holdings and ventures in crypto, which are run by his sons, according to the president’s financial disclosure forms reviewed by Fox News Digital. Curtis noted that nearly three-quarters of Americans believed the federal government to be corrupt, and that the issue of rooting out corruption shouldn’t be a partisan matter. REPUBLICANS TARGET TRUMP'S CRYPTO EMPIRE WITH NEW PLAN, DEMS SAY IT FALLS SHORT "The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president," Curtis wrote. "Nor should congressional oversight begin and end when control of the White House changes hands." Republicans launched probe after probe into Hunter Biden’s business dealings and whether his father, former President Joe Biden, was involved. Curtis acknowledged that Biden "has denied involving his father in his business dealings," but countered that his father being in office "opened doors that otherwise may have remained closed." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The same, Curtis argued, goes for Trump Jr. "These reports raise legitimate questions about foreign access to members of a sitting president's family and whether such relationships can create actual or perceived expectations of favorable treatment," Curtis wrote. "They also may create expectations of a returned favor that would not be in the best interests of the American people or our allies, and could even create national security vulnerabilities."Fox News Digital did not receive immediate comment from the Trump Organization, White House nor Hunter Biden by publication.

articles.title: Terry Moran says network rejected his Biden health story after he witnessed president’s frailty
articles.summary: Terry Moran says ABC News leadership shut down his pitch to report on former President Joe Biden's declining health, telling him the story wasn't his to cover.
articles.body: Former ABC News correspondent Terry Moran revealed Monday that he tried to report on concerns about then-President Joe Biden's declining health — but was promptly shut down by senior leadership at the network. "In late 2023, early 2024, you know, it was pretty clear that Biden was fading rather quickly," Moran told The Daily Beast podcast. "I had actually traveled with him to Japan in the spring of 2023 and kind of eyeballed him there, and I thought, 'Okay, he’s still functioning, but man, he’s frail.’ He looked like he’d blow away in a stiff wind." Moran added that the now-83-year-old former president’s voice was merely a "whisper" by his final year in office. EX-ABC NEWS CORRESPONDENT CLAIMS NETWORK OVERHAULED HIS COVID LAB LEAK REPORT AFTER SENDING COPY TO FAUCI "I tried to do the story of Biden’s health before anybody else did in network, because I’d seen it," Moran said. "And I got shut down very hard." Moran said he sent an email pitch to his editors for a story about Biden’s declining health "gently and as respectfully" as possible. "It was like, ‘You know, this is [a] legit issue for Americans to be interested in,’" Moran said. "I'm not a doctor. I'm not diagnosing. But we all know what we know when we see people fading. We all have had grandparents. We're all getting old ourselves. And so there's no doubt about it, this is a legitimate concern for the voters of America." EX-CBS REPORTER CLAIMS QUESTIONING FAUCI GOT HER 'PULLED OFF AIR' DURING COVID PANDEMIC However, Moran said that ABC News’ leadership allegedly shot down the pitch, telling him the then-president’s health is "the medical unit’s business, not yours." Fox News Digital reached out to ABC News for comment but did not immediately receive a response. Moran — a veteran correspondent at the outlet — left ABC News following a social media post in which he attacked President Donald Trump and White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller. Moran called Trump and Miller "world-class haters" in the now-deleted post on X. "We are at the end of our agreement with Terry Moran and based on his recent post — which was a clear violation of ABC News policies — we have made the decision to not renew," a spokesperson for ABC News confirmed to Fox News Digital at the time. ABC HAS NO BUSINESS ON PUBLIC AIRWAVES BECAUSE IT OPERATES 'LIKE A PARTISAN CABLE NETWORK,’ WATCHDOG TELLS FCC The topic of Biden's health and mental acuity while president received renewed attention following his departure from office, including books and reports alleging that aides concealed the extent of his decline. Some mainstream media outlets have also drawn criticism over their coverage of questions about the then-president's mental acuity, with CNN anchor Jake Tapper and Axios reporter Alex Thompson co-authoring "Original Sin: President Biden's Decline, Its Cover-Up, and His Disastrous Choice to Run Again," which draws on more than 200 interviews and argues that Biden's inner circle concealed signs of decline from the public. Moran's attempt to report on Biden's health — and his account that ABC News declined the pitch — was noted by psychotherapist Jonathan Alpert, who told Fox News Digital the veteran journalist was simply doing his due diligence as a reporter. "Moran was doing exactly what reporters are paid to do: he noticed something and wanted to ask questions about it," Alpert said. "You don’t have to diagnose Biden to report that he appeared different. We make observations about people every day without knowing the medical explanation for them. Saying ‘I see a change’ and saying ‘I know what’s causing that change’ are completely different statements." According to Alpert, it’s "also a very human tendency to avoid information that creates a problem for us," adding that, "sometimes it’s easier not to look too closely and that seems to be exactly what ABC was doing." LIBERAL CNN ANCHOR LASHES OUT AT DEMOCRATS' DECEIT AFTER JILL BIDEN'S ADMISSION ABOUT JOE'S DEBATE SHOWING "I think what ultimately hurts credibility is the gap between what the public thinks is obvious and what an institution is willing to acknowledge," Alpert told Fox News Digital. "The wider that gap gets, the more people start wondering whether they're getting the whole story. A journalist's job is to be willing to ask the questions, even without knowing all the answers." articles.title: Trump-backed Senate candidate says 'Groceries cost too much,' calls for Iran war to 'end quickly'
articles.summary: Trump-backed Michigan Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers declared in a video that "Groceries cost too much" and the Iran war "needs to end, and end quickly."
articles.body: Former Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican Michigan U.S. Senate candidate backed by President Donald Trump, noted the financial strain Americans are facing, declared that the Iran war must "end quickly," and called for a diesel export embargo until the conflict concludes in a social media video. "Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life. Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down. The war with Iran needs to end, and end quickly. When it does, energy costs will plummet. But Michigan families can’t afford to wait for that to happen," Rogers said in the video. "I previously called for the suspension of the state and federal gas tax, 70 cents a gallon," he said. The state's motor fuel tax, which applies to both gas and diesel, is 52.4 cents per gallon. "Federal taxes include excise taxes of 18.3 cents per gallon on gasoline and 24.3 cents per gallon on diesel fuel, and a Leaking Underground Storage Tank fee of 0.1 cents per gallon on both fuels," according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. ANXIETY GROWS OVER EMERGING ELECTION ISSUE, BUT GOP SAYS WASHINGTON ISN'T THE ANSWER While Rogers does not appear to have called for a suspension of the federal diesel tax, he called for a diesel export embargo. "Diesel fuels the trucks that bring groceries to this store. It fuels the tractors that grow our food. And when diesel costs more, it costs more to grow it, ship it, stock it, and ultimately, buy it. So until this war is over, I’m calling for a temporary embargo on American diesel exports," he said. Trump has endorsed Rogers, including in a video posted last week on social media. "Mike Rogers has my Complete and Total Endorsement to be the next U.S. Senator from Michigan — HE WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!" the video's caption read. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House on Tuesday. The AAA national average price for diesel is at a record high of $6.5276 as of Sept. 22. EL-SAYED'S JEWISH OUTREACH IGNITES 'TOKENISM' FURY AS MICHIGAN GOP CHAIR MAKES BOLD PREDICTION Rogers is running against Democratic Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. Responding to Rogers' video, El-Sayed targeted his Republican rival in a post on X, writing, "You've spent your entire campaign supporting the war in Iran. Liar, coward, fraud." Former Rep. Justin Amash, who finished the 2024 GOP Michigan U.S. Senate primary in a distant second place behind Rogers, wrote in a post on X, "When inveterate war hawk Mike Rogers suddenly declares, 'The war in Iran needs to end—and end quickly,' you know he’s losing—and losing badly." Fox News Digital reached out to Rogers' campaign on Tuesday.
